cases.question: How did the 2026 interim dividend affect CBA's CET1 ratio during the June 2026 half, and what role did the Dividend Reinvestment Plan play?
gold_answer_facts: The dividend reduced CET1 by 76bps on the Dec 25 -> Jun 26 walk, shown 'DRP neutralised'
The DRP was satisfied IN FULL by on-market share purchases — no new shares were issued
The interim-dividend DRP purchase was $530m, itself costing 10bps of CET1 (inside the 76)
DRP participation rates: 14.8% (2025 final) and 13.5% (2026 interim)

required_locations.holds: the -76bps dividend bar and footnote 2 ($530m on-market, -10bps)
DRP satisfied in full on-market; participation rates

cases.trap: Reading only the walk yields '-76bps' and misses that the bank spent capital to neutralise the DRP and that no shares were issued — the footnote and the PA text change the interpretation.

cases.question: CBA's reported NIM is calculated net of mortgage offset account balances. Quantify those balances for FY26 and FY25 and explain how they affect average interest earning assets and NIM.
gold_answer_facts: Average mortgage offset balances: $94,892m FY26; $84,123m FY25; $97,371m for the Jun 26 half vs $92,454m for the Dec 25 half
The balances are grossed up under accounting standards but netted down for calculating customer interest payments and the Group's NIM
Home loan average interest earning assets are therefore shown net of offsets

required_locations.holds: footnote 1 under the NII table — the only place the offset figures exist

cases.trap: The answer lives entirely in a table footnote that page-level extraction typically skips; there is no chart or section heading pointing at it.

cases.question: Name CBA's FY26 notable and restructuring items, quantify them in total, and state their effect on operating expense growth and the cost-to-income ratio (headline vs underlying).
gold_answer_facts: Total restructuring and notable items: $170m (FY25 comparable framing: $130m implied by the benchmark's delta; FY25 items were domestic/NZ remediation and a Bankwest restructuring provision)
FY26 items: provisions for the settlement of legal proceedings in NZ; an additional goodwill payment to certain customers from ASIC's Better Banking review; domestic customer remediation
Underlying expense growth +5.6% vs headline +5.8% including these items
Headline CTI 45.5% (vs 45.7% FY25); the underlying CTI framing appears on the expense slide

required_locations.holds: the $170m line and footnote 2 naming the items
footnote 1: underlying vs headline (+5.6% vs +5.8%) framing
the KPI table's CTI row (45.5 vs 45.7)

cases.trap: The value, the item names, the growth-rate framing, and the ratio effect live on three different pages across two documents; each alone gives an incomplete or misleading answer.
